content.title: What is HTML?
content.text: HTML stands for HyperText Markup Language. It is used to structure the content of web pages.

content.title: HTML Elements
content.text: HTML documents are made up of elements. Elements are commonly written using an opening tag, content and a closing tag.

content.title: Attributes
content.text: Attributes provide additional information about an HTML element and are normally written inside the opening tag.

lessons.title: HTML Document Structure

content.title: Basic Document
content.text: An HTML document normally contains a DOCTYPE declaration, an html element, a head section and a body section.

content.title: Head
content.text: The head contains information about the document such as its title, metadata and links to external resources.

content.title: Body
content.text: The body contains the visible content of the web page.

key_points: The body contains visible page content.

lessons.title: Text, Headings and Lists

content.title: Headings
content.text: HTML provides six heading levels from h1 to h6. h1 represents the highest-level heading.

content.title: Paragraphs
content.text: The p element is used to represent a paragraph of text.

content.title: Lists
content.text: Unordered lists use ul and li elements. Ordered lists use ol and li elements.

key_points: Use h1 through h6 for headings.

content.title: Links
content.text: The anchor element creates hyperlinks. The href attribute specifies the destination.

content.title: Images
content.text: The img element displays an image. The src attribute specifies the image source and alt provides alternative text.

content.title: Tables
content.text: Tables use table, tr, th and td elements to represent tabular data.

lessons.title: Semantic HTML

content.title: Semantic Elements
content.text: Semantic HTML elements describe the purpose of their content instead of using generic containers everywhere.

content.title: Why Semantic HTML?
content.text: Semantic markup improves document structure, accessibility and maintainability.

key_points: main represents the main page content.

lessons.title: HTML Forms

content.title: Forms
content.text: HTML forms allow users to enter information that can be submitted to a server.

content.title: Input Types
content.text: The input element supports different types such as text, email, password, number, date and checkbox.

content.title: Input Types
content.code:
<input type="email" name="email">
<input type="password" name="password">
<input type="number" name="age">
<input type="checkbox" name="agree">

content.title: Labels
content.text: Labels describe form controls and improve usability and accessibility.

key_points: Input type determines the kind of data expected.

lessons.title: HTML5 and Modern HTML

content.title: HTML5
content.text: HTML5 introduced many semantic elements and native support for multimedia and modern web applications.

content.title: Accessibility
content.text: Good HTML should be structured clearly and use appropriate labels, alternative text and semantic elements.

key_points: HTML5 provides modern semantic and multimedia features.
Audio and video can be embedded natively.
Accessible HTML uses meaningful structure and labels.

lessons.title: Building a Basic Web Page

content.title: Putting It Together
content.text: A basic web page combines document structure, semantic elements, text, links, images and forms.

content.title: Next Step
content.text: HTML provides the structure of a web page. CSS is then used to control its visual appearance and layout.

key_points: CSS can be added to style the HTML.
JavaScript can later add behavior and interactivity.
